title: Weekly email digest render holding order rows

verification.methodology: pact business verification (database + checkout SLO + protected ops)

checks.name: database_clear

audit.report: The weekly email digest render job (batch_replayable_email_digest_render, pid 1297011) held locks that blocked checkout, causing 120/120 checkouts to fail over 30 seconds with $18,400/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian initially proposed waiting since the blocker had only been idle for 4.2s, but after querying the workload registry and business impact, switched to termination when trade-off analysis showed waiting would cost ~$256,312 and exceed the 60-second business tolerance. The Continuity Guardian accepted the termination, noting the job is BATCH_REPLAYABLE with a 5-minute replay cost and may_interrupt policy. The authority authorized the action, the executor terminated the blocker, and verification confirmed checkout recovered to 100% success (36/36) with no lock waits and no protected settlements affected. The business is back.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_email_digest_render job (pid 1297011) held a transaction open while idle, blocking checkout sessions and causing complete checkout failure.
lessons: For batch_replayable_email_digest_render: ensure the workload registry entry (class BATCH_REPLAYABLE, replayable=True, replay cost 5 min, policy may_interrupt) is pre-registered so the Database Guardian doesn't need to probe it during an incident.

For batch_replayable_email_digest_render: add a transaction timeout or idle-in-transaction guard to prevent it from holding locks indefinitely while idle (last statement was SELECT 1 for 4.2s before detection).
For batch_replayable_email_digest_render: configure monitoring to alert when this job runs longer than its typical 840s runtime, since it blocks checkout when it holds locks.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian wasted no rounds — it proposed wait initially due to missing registry/tradeoff data, then immediately probed for and used that evidence to switch to terminate in the same round, leading to a single-round pact. The Continuity Guardian correctly accepted based on the quantified trade-off.
follow_ups: Add batch_replayable_email_digest_render to the workload registry with its BATCH_REPLAYABLE class, 5-minute replay cost, and may_interrupt policy before the next incident.
Investigate why batch_replayable_email_digest_render was idle in transaction with SELECT 1 for 4.2s and add an idle-in-transaction timeout for batch_worker connections.
Add a runtime alert for batch_replayable_email_digest_render when it exceeds its typical 840s runtime to catch blocking earlier.

proposal.rationale: The root blocker (pid 1297011, batch_replayable_email_digest_render) is idle in transaction for only 4.2s with last statement SELECT 1, suggesting it may complete soon. Terminating an unknown workload risks data integrity or replay cost without evidence from biz.workload_registry (MISSING) or biz.tradeoff (MISSING). Memory MEM-1 shows a different job (product_feed_rebuild) was safely terminated, but this is email_digest_render — not the same workload. Business impact is severe (BIZ-1: 82% success vs 95% SLO, $3,286/min at risk, 60s tolerance), but acting blindly could worsen blast radius. Requesting missing probes to inform a safe terminate/escalate decision in the next round.
proposal.expected_effect: No immediate change to database locks; checkout remains degraded while blocker runs. If blocker completes quickly (<60s total degradation), checkout recovers automatically. If not, probe results will enable a targeted terminate or escalate in round 2.
proposal.risk_assessment: Blocker may not finish within business tolerance (60s), extending checkout degradation and revenue loss. Idle-in-transaction sessions often indicate application bugs or external waits that won't self-resolve. Waiting without a fallback plan risks exceeding the 60s threshold.
